definition: Brownian motion (or Wiener process) is a mathematical description of random motion, independently developed in botany (Robert Brown) and physics (Norbert Wiener), that characterizes the boundaries of a random walk made up of very small steps.
core_idea: It is the mathematical foundation used to model continuous random price movement in option pricing.
key_points: Same underlying mathematical process was discovered independently in two different scientific fields.
Describes the limiting behavior of a random walk taken in very small increments.
relationships: Related to random walk and stochastic process
